definitions.explanation: Genuine mirin made by fermenting glutinous rice and rice koji with shochu. Contains about 14% alcohol, distinguishing it from low-alcohol mirin-style seasonings.

examples.japanese: {本|ほん}みりん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
{本|ほん}みりん⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{照|て}り→照り：16401_teri⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{深|ふか}い→深い：01211_fukai⟧⟦{甘|あま}み→甘み：17244_amami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: True mirin produces glaze and a deep sweetness.

examples.japanese: {本|ほん}みりん⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦アルコール→アルコール：01771_arukooru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{含|ふく}む→含む：01982_fukumu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{始|はじ}め⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{加|くわ}えて→加える：01941_kuwaeru⟧{煮切|にき}ること⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Since true mirin contains alcohol, it's often added at the start of cooking and boiled to evaporate the alcohol.

notes:
Distinguished from みりん{風|ふう}⟦{調味料|ちょうみりょう}→調味料：04941_choumiryou⟧ (mirin-style seasoning), which contains little or no alcohol and is cheaper. {本|ほん}みりん is treated as an alcoholic beverage in Japan and is sold in the liquor section.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {本|ほん}みりん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{加|くわ}える→加える：01941_kuwaeru⟧: to add true mirin
- {本|ほん}みりん⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{煮|に}る→煮る：01971_niru⟧: to simmer with true mirin
- {本|ほん}みりん⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{照|て}り→照り：16401_teri⟧: the glaze produced by true mirin

SIMILAR WORDS:
- みりん{風|ふう}⟦{調味料|ちょうみりょう}→調味料：04941_choumiryou⟧: mirin-style seasoning — low-alcohol substitute, milder flavor
- ⟦{料理酒|りょうりしゅ}→料理酒：17180_ryourishu⟧: cooking sake — adds depth but lacks sweetness
